video_title: Cyberattacks Used to Take Months. AI Can Do It in Minutes.
gist: Wiz's Ammy argues 'Black October' marks the arrival of real AI attacks: frontier and fast-catching-up open source models now find and exploit vulnerabilities (e.g. PHP-to-shell) and run full attacks in ~20 minutes, while patching lags. The answer is continuous AI self-attack (red agent) focused on external exposure, cost-efficient multi-model pipelines, secure design over budget, and dropping non-security work.

themes.theme: Black October: AI attacks go live

insights.claim: Wiz calls October 2026 'Black October', a black-swan month with an unprecedented number and severity of vulnerabilities plus the rise of real AI-driven attacks on companies, startups and even refrigerators.
insights.speaker: Ammy (Wiz)
insights.so_what: Security incident volume has stepped up structurally; expect demand pull for AI-native security vendors and rising breach headlines.
insights.quote: we've never seen never ever seen so many um security incidents happen in a single month

insights.claim: The path to Black October ran through two warning moments: the 'Mitos' model showing AI could find vulnerabilities, and an accidental Hugging Face incident involving OpenAI; in October those theories materialized at once.
insights.speaker: Ammy (Wiz)
insights.so_what: Frontier-model capability releases are now leading indicators for security incident waves.

insights.claim: Frontier models are now good enough to find AND exploit complex vulnerabilities, and an attack chain that took the best human attackers weeks or months now runs in around 20 minutes.
insights.speaker: Ammy (Wiz)
insights.so_what: Detection-and-response windows measured in hours are obsolete; value shifts to automated, minute-scale response.
insights.quote: basically run an entire attack that usually took for the best attackers weeks or months in again around 20 minutes

insights.claim: Open source models are catching up on offensive capability far faster than expected: Wiz thinks frontier advantage in vulnerability finding is no more than ~3 months, versus a16z hearing 6-9 months and an earlier hope of a year.
insights.speaker: Ammy (Wiz)
insights.so_what: Commoditized offensive AI means unsophisticated attackers get elite capability; the defender's lead from frontier-model access is thin.
insights.quote: the hope was that open source models are a year behind but they're not

insights.claim: AI is arguably the only domain where AI is already better than humans: AI attacks are prevalent, easy and better than any human, e.g. a kernel-driver zero-day attack that should be rare is now happening daily.
insights.speaker: Ammy (Wiz)
insights.so_what: Offense has superhuman capability before defense does; frames a multi-year asymmetric threat cycle favoring security spend.
insights.quote: this is almost the only area in humankind right now that AI is better than humans

insights.claim: The PHP-to-shell vulnerability, discovered independently by Wiz and Califf, is probably the most severe vulnerability ever found by AI, and almost 100% of Wiz customers had some PHP running.
insights.speaker: Ammy (Wiz)
insights.so_what: Single AI-found bugs can now hit near-universal attack surfaces; watch for remediation spend spikes.

insights.claim: After the PHP disclosure about 50% of affected Wiz customers patched within the first 2-3 days, but because PHP is ~70% of the internet and older versions get no patch, this single vulnerability will take years to resolve.
insights.speaker: Ammy (Wiz)
insights.so_what: Long tail of unpatchable legacy exposure creates persistent breach risk and sustained demand for exposure management.
insights.quote: is going to take years okay until it's resolved

insights.claim: Time to weaponize a patch into an exploit has collapsed while time to patch has not fallen (it has risen over 20-25 years); information often leaks before the CVE or patch, as happened with PHP despite months of coordinated work.
insights.speaker: Ammy (Wiz)
insights.so_what: The exploit-vs-patch asymmetry is widening; vendors that shrink time-to-remediate capture value.

insights.claim: Linux kernel fixes can take weeks or months to reach all distros, so even companies that patch quickly internally are blocked; the industry is 'not ready' for minute-scale AI exploitation.
insights.speaker: Ammy (Wiz)
insights.so_what: Upstream supply-chain latency in patching is a structural weakness that no single buyer can fix.
insights.quote: the world is not ready. The world is not ready for this

insights.claim: Ammy sees no clear path to automated patching for legacy companies, but new startups should design for auto-patch with a fully agentic pipeline: automated dev from ticket, automated testing, CI/CD and DevOps.
insights.speaker: Ammy (Wiz)
insights.so_what: Greenfield companies with agentic SDLC gain a security advantage; tooling for automated remediation is a startup opportunity.
insights.quote: for new companies, you should design your system to be able to auto patch

insights.claim: Vulnerability discovery is like Bitcoin mining: each new model uncovers more bugs, so multiple teams will increasingly find the same vulnerabilities at once, as Wiz sees with multiple reports of a critical bug ahead of its ZDC zero-day competition.
insights.speaker: Ammy (Wiz)
insights.so_what: Each frontier model release likely triggers a new wave of disclosures; time security budgets and positions to model launches.
insights.quote: I look at it like Bitcoin mining

themes.theme: Multi-model pipelines and AI security unit economics

insights.claim: Wiz runs Atlas, an internal vulnerability-detection harness, across many models from OpenAI, Google and others because each model and each cyber-tuned version behaves differently in capability, speed and cost.
insights.speaker: Ammy (Wiz)
insights.so_what: Independent security vendors stay model-agnostic even inside Google; frontier labs are suppliers, not sole winners.

insights.claim: The key engineering challenge for AI companies at scale is cost: a scalable service requires intelligent pipelines that route simple tasks to cheap models and hard ones to expensive models, otherwise you lose money on sales.
insights.speaker: Ammy (Wiz)
insights.so_what: Gross margin of AI-native software depends on model routing; evaluate startups on pipeline efficiency, not just model access.
insights.quote: otherwise you're you're you're going to lose money on on your sales

insights.claim: Wiz's blue agent escalates through deterministic detection, then a cheap model, then a more advanced model, and only invokes the most advanced model to confirm maliciousness before alerting the customer.
insights.speaker: Ammy (Wiz)
insights.so_what: Tiered-inference architecture is a template for cost-efficient AI SOC products.

insights.claim: Brute-force code scanning with frontier models is very expensive: a company that scanned all its code after the Mitos moment in April might have wasted $5 million and must redo it with each new model like Mitos 1.2, and some customers now spend tens of millions on code scanning.
insights.speaker: Ammy (Wiz)
insights.so_what: Huge new spend is flowing to AI code scanning, but much is inefficient; vendors that optimize continuous scanning budgets win.
insights.quote: some customers are spending now tens of millions of dollars on like scanning code

themes.theme: Red agent: continuous self-attack beats code scanning

insights.claim: Defenses must become dynamic because every new model raises the attacker 'watermark': an application secure yesterday may not be secure today, so companies must continuously attack themselves with the latest models.
insights.speaker: Ammy (Wiz)
insights.so_what: Continuous AI red-teaming / attack-surface testing is becoming a must-have budget line.
insights.quote: whatever was considered secure last week, if every AI model can get into the door, it's not secure anymore

insights.claim: Wiz's red-side pipeline starts with deterministic exposure analysis, then an exposure agent spending minutes per endpoint on unauthenticated internet-facing surfaces, then deep pentests taking up to 10 hours on critical applications, with unfixable findings handed to the blue agent for detections.
insights.speaker: Ammy (Wiz)
insights.so_what: Integrated red/blue platforms create cross-sell and lock-in; tiered compute budgeting is the moat.

insights.claim: The majority of Wiz customers already use the red agent, approaching full coverage, making it one of the fastest growing features Wiz has ever released.
insights.speaker: Ammy (Wiz)
insights.so_what: Strong adoption signal for AI offensive-security products inside Google's Wiz; read-through for competing exposure-management vendors.
insights.quote: it's really one of the fastest growing features that we've ever released

insights.claim: Ammy argues the Mitos PR pushed the market toward code scanning, which is not the most efficient spend; scanning unauthenticated external exposure continuously matters more, as shown by a recent breach from a key hardcoded in a mobile app.
insights.speaker: Ammy (Wiz)
insights.so_what: Budget may rotate from AI code-scanning toward external attack-surface management; pick vendors accordingly.
insights.quote: I actually don't think the scanning code is the most efficient thing you can do

themes.theme: Startups and AI platforms as prime targets

insights.claim: AI development platforms are being specifically targeted because they hold AI keys: Wiz's blog initially listed nine such companies attacked in October and the list has grown to 15.
insights.speaker: Ammy (Wiz)
insights.so_what: AI dev-tool startups carry outsized breach risk; diligence their security posture and key management.

insights.claim: Startups holding AI keys are now attackers' key target for LLM hijacking, and a whole attack from entry to stealing all customers' secrets and AI keys takes about 20 minutes, so startups effectively need a 24/7 SOC.
insights.speaker: Ammy (Wiz)
insights.so_what: Demand for managed/automated SOC for small companies; founders should cap API key spend limits immediately.
insights.quote: Startups are actually their key target now for for LLM checking

insights.claim: a16z's Zayn and Joel advised portfolio founders during Black October to spend more on security and consider delaying releases, while Zayn argues the new model is running security in parallel via blue and red agents rather than delaying ships.
insights.speaker: Zayn (a16z)
insights.so_what: VC-level guidance signals portfolio-wide security spend increases.

themes.theme: Security budgets, design and obsolete tools

insights.claim: A CISO told a16z he expects his security budget to rise 80% next year, at the high end of expected increases.
insights.speaker: host (a16z)
insights.so_what: Security budgets are inflecting upward sharply; supportive for cybersecurity vendor revenue in 2027.

insights.claim: Ammy argues budget alone won't solve AI-era risk; it is about secure design: sandboxes, isolation, network/process/image lockdown, and assuming container escapes since Linux zero-days are constant.
insights.speaker: Ammy (Wiz)
insights.so_what: Favors isolation/sandboxing and secure-architecture vendors over point tools.
insights.quote: if you're building stuff now, get ready for a nation state attacker

insights.claim: Most legacy security tools are no longer relevant, and classic CSPM configuration-check lists are low value compared with understanding where the attacker will come from.
insights.speaker: Ammy (Wiz)
insights.so_what: Legacy security vendors and checklist-style CSPM face displacement by AI-native platforms.
insights.quote: Obviously most of the legacy security tools are not even relevant anymore

insights.claim: Zayn sees CISOs rebooting their vendor stacks toward AI-native tools in a step change similar to the cloud transition.
insights.speaker: Zayn (a16z)
insights.so_what: Expect a vendor replacement cycle benefiting AI-native security startups.

insights.claim: Most of what security teams do (compliance, reports) is not security; teams should focus solely on finding critical risk, mitigating or adding detections, and response readiness.
insights.speaker: Ammy (Wiz)
insights.so_what: Compliance-automation and reporting tools may lose budget share to risk-reduction tooling.
insights.quote: Most of what security teams do is not security

insights.claim: Customers now expect Wiz to go beyond prioritized findings: trace back to code, generate the fix and pull request, and run full investigations and forensics; the next step is automated response, which Ammy calls scary but unavoidable.
insights.speaker: Ammy (Wiz)
insights.so_what: Security platforms are expanding into remediation and autonomous response, enlarging TAM.

insights.claim: Legacy enterprises with thousands of developers and unclear resource ownership will take time to reach security automation because organizational knowledge is undocumented, while new companies can build fully automated security from scratch.
insights.speaker: Ammy (Wiz)
insights.so_what: Asset-ownership/context tooling is a bottleneck and an opportunity.
insights.quote: If I cannot respond in minutes

themes.theme: Next 2-3 years: back to the wild west

insights.claim: Zayn predicts security is going back to the 1990s-2000s with constant unauthenticated full RCEs, frequent breaches, and possibly internet worms like the Windows XP era when systems were infected before they could be patched.
insights.speaker: Zayn (a16z)
insights.so_what: Breach frequency likely to rise for years, sustaining security spend and incident-response demand.
insights.quote: I wouldn't be surprised if we end up seeing worms again on the internet

insights.claim: Ammy thinks Black October may be just the beginning, worse than the 90s because dependency on technology is far higher, and only companies redesigning internet-exposed systems should survive; unready systems should be taken off the internet.
insights.speaker: Ammy (Wiz)
insights.so_what: Expect forced attack-surface reduction and existential risk for laggard internet-facing businesses.
insights.quote: whatever is not ready should take take off the internet

insights.claim: Connected legacy public infrastructure such as refrigeration units in Europe and traffic systems is at risk; Wiz launched Scan for Good to scan public services and nudge them to start their own red scanning.
insights.speaker: Ammy (Wiz)
insights.so_what: Public-sector and OT/IoT security are under-funded exposures likely to draw policy and spending.
